items.title: GPT 6 is being pitched on knowledge per dollar instead of benchmark scores, and that one change tells you more than any
items.summary:
GPT 6 is being pitched on knowledge per dollar instead of benchmark scores, and that one change tells you more than any leaked capability list!

benchmark scores → capability claims → autonomy duration → cost per unit of knowledge

Benchmarks measure what a model does once, under ideal conditions, with a human watching.

Knowledge per dollar measures what it produces per unit of spend across long unsupervised runs.

Those two numbers stop agreeing the moment a model runs for hours instead of turns.

A model that is 5% worse and 70% cheaper wins every workload you run continuously.

The frame changed because the buyer changed, from researchers picking a winner to operators picking a cost curve.

Watch which number Sam Altman leads with in Washington. 

It tells you who he thinks is paying.

Everyone is still arguing about which model is smartest.

The people running agents all day stopped caring about that a while ago.

Follow @neil_xbt for more!

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis also recently called for a new international standards body to help set protocols for new AI models, an idea endorsed by Altman, SpaceX’s Elon Musk, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other major industry figures. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

items.title: House Panel Weighs AI Job Gains Against Worker Risks
items.summary:
In April 2025, President Trump signed an executive order creating a White House task force on AI education and directing the Secretary of Labor to expand AI-related Registered Apprenticeships. The administration's AI Action Plan directs the Department of Labor to prioritize AI skill development across workforce funding streams and proposes an AI Workforce Research Hub. Beginning July 1, students became eligible for Pell Grants covering short-term programs in high-skill, in-demand fields. [...] ## The Bottom Line

Eight hearings in, the committee has built a case for AI as an opportunity engine without producing legislation that reconciles it with what Barlow and McBath described. Augusta made the tension concrete: the same technology anchoring a biomanufacturing plant and a new medical AI department also requires transmission lines running through civilians' properties.

Access the Legis1 platform for comprehensive political news, data, and insights. [...] ## What's Next

Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) introduced the AI Workforce Training Act in February, creating a 30 percent tax credit for employer-provided AI training. Sen. Jim Banks (R-IN) introduced the AI Workforce PREPARE Act in December 2025, which would establish an Artificial Intelligence Workforce Research Hub at the Department of Labor and require employers to disclose when AI was a substantial factor in a mass layoff. Both remain in committee.

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

I asked @jxnlco (DevEx at OpenAI): “What’s the craziest thing Codex did for you?”

Here’s his answer:

“I was on a bike ride when a coworker asked me to fix a launch video. So I connected remotely from my phone and asked Codex to use computer use to edit the video, export it, and post it back to Slack.

Twenty minutes later, there was a new video in the Slack thread. Then I told Codex:

‘Every 30 minutes, check the thread for feedback and export V2, V3, V4.’

By the time I got home, the launch video was greenlit.”

Codex had handled the revisions by repeatedly checking Slack for feedback.

items.title: 『2026-07-29 日本市場デイリー・リキャップ：AIデレバレッジ継続、日経平均1.49％安』
items.summary:
『2026-07-29 日本市場デイリー・リキャップ：AIデレバレッジ継続、日経平均1.49％安』

　当日の東京市場における中核的な見立ては、元レポートの「日経平均は約2.6％下落」から、日経平均は1.49％安の61,434.19ptで終了、約2ヶ月ぶりの水準となり、半導体セクターが最大の下落要因となった、と修正すべきである。真の主下落は前営業日（7月28日）に発生しており、当日の日経平均は3.95％安の62,364.92pt、東京エレクトロンは10.96％安、アドバンテストは10％超安、ソフトバンクは4.43％安、キオクシアは18.33％安となった。7月29日の-1.49％はパニック放出後の慣性消化に過ぎず、新たな下落加速ではない。元レポートは両日の下落幅を混同し、単日の圧力を誇張している。ドライビング・ロジックは以下の通り：米国主要テクノロジー企業の決算公表を前に、市場がAI設備投資（キャッペックス）の投資収益率に疑問を呈し、中東戦火の再燃がリスク選好を抑制、アジアのチップ株は一斉に売りにさらされた。

　クロスアセットおよび資金面：USD/JPY、10年JGB利回り、TOPIX終値、東証REIT、CME日経先物、EWJ/DXJ/BBJP、bitFlyer/Coincheck出来高、JPX当日の外国人売買速報、Nikkei VI、プット／コール・レシオ、信用買い残、空売り比率、値上がり・値下がり銘柄数――上記のうち元レポートが「未公表」としていた項目について、公開検索ソースでも7月29日当日のデータは提供されておらず、「未公表」のままとする。補足的に引用可能な背景データとしては、JPXの5月前三週間における東証プライム市場の平均売買代金が初めて10兆円を突破し、個人投資家の売買構成比が約25％（ジェフリーズがPTSを合算した試算では約39％）であったことがあり、「機関が方向性を定め、個人がボラティリティを生む」という構造的特徴を示すが、このデータは5月時点のものであり、7月29日当日の資金行動に外挿することはできない。東京エレクトロンのADRは7月29日に米国株市場で10.08％安、アドバンテストADRは5.85％安となったが、これは米国時間のクオートであり、東京市場の現地株終値と同一視できない。引用の際はその旨を注記する必要がある。

　テクニカル水準と翌日のシナリオ：元レポートが示した日経平均の支持63,500–64,000、抵抗65,500–66,000というレンジは、当日終値61,434ptに対してアンカリングに乖離がある――実際の終値はその支持下限を約2,000pt下回っており、翌日に真に観察すべきは61,000の整数関門と、6月22日の史上最高値72,831ptからの調整チャネル下限での受け止めであり、65,500の「ブレイクアウト・買い増し」シグナルではない。USD/JPY 164の圧力水準、BOJのタカ派／ハト派が銀行株と成長株に及ぼす非対称的な影響、FOMCシグナルが世界の成長株バリュエーションに与える伝播効果は、いずれも翌日の合理的な観察変数である。セクターレベルでは、半導体製造装置株（東京エレクトロン、アドバンテスト、SCREEN）の買いポイントのトリガーは「VWAP回帰」といった短期的シグナルではなく、米国SOX指数の下落止まり＋AIキャッペックス見通しの明確化という二つの前提条件の少なくとも一方が満たされるのを待つべきである。

#日経平均 #TOPIX #BOJ #FOMC #USDJPY #JGB #東京エレクトロン #アドバンテスト #ソフトバンク #キオクシア #AIキャッペックス #半導体 #SOX #フィラデルフィア半導体指数 #KKR #中東リスク #インフレトレード #リスクオフ #日本株 #外国人資金フロー #個人投資家 #PTS #EWJ #DXJ #BBJP #REIT #VWAP 

【見解】：元レポートの方向性判断（AIデレバレッジ→半導体が足を引っ張る→日経平均が下落を主導）は市場の実際と一致するが、中核データに日付のズレがある：7月28日の単日3.95％安というパニック売りと、7月29日の1.49％安という慣性消化を混同したことで、「日経平均は約2.6％下落」という不正確な表現が生まれ、またテクニカル水準を65,500台にアンカーしたことは、実際の終値61,434ptという現実から大きく乖離している。信頼度は7/10――ストーリー・フレームワークは利用可能だが、数字は修正後にしか取引の指針となり得ない。主要リスクは三つ：第一に、東京エレクトロン／アドバンテストの現地株の下落幅は公開ソースでは完全に開示されておらず、ADRクオートは代替にならないこと。第二に、JPXの投資家分類日次データが7月29日時点で更新されておらず、外国人が連続して売り越しているか判断できないこと。第三に、元レポートが「未公表」項目を確定項目と並列に提示することで、読者に情報の完全度を過大評価させる恐れがあること。意思決定の含意：翌日のメイン戦略「AIチェーンの下落止まりを待つ」は有効だが、具体的なトリガー水準は61,000関門と60,000の心理的水準に下方修正すべきであり、65,500は「ブレイクアウト・買い増し」ではなく「トレンド反転の確認」により適したシグナルとなる。FOMCとBOJの政策シグナルは真の外部変数であり、これら二つのイベントが確定する前は、あらゆるテクニカルな買いポイントはトレンド取引ではなくリバウンド取引に過ぎない。

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: OpenAI's $1 Trillion IPO Ambition Faces New Timing Test as Anthropic Gains Ground - Dailyhunt
items.summary: **OpenAI** may be pushing back its public debut as it weighs whether market conditions can support its reported goal of a $1 trillion valuation. The analysts noted that OpenAI's decision on timing effectively acts as a pricing signal: management must choose between going public sooner at a potentially discounted valuation or waiting longer in hopes of reaching the $1 trillion mark. Despite OpenAI's higher valuation (private market valuations of $852 billion), PitchBook ($965 billion) suggested Anthropic currently commands a more attractive valuation relative to its business quality score. PitchBook said investors should watch for OpenAI to convert its confidential filing into a public S-1, the pricing of its employee tender offer, SpaceX’s Aug. 6 earnings and lockup timeline, and whether Anthropic proceeds with an October IPO. The firm said its outlook would change if OpenAI moves ahead with a 2026 IPO or if its public S-1 shows investors are willing to support a $1 trillion valuation sooner than expected.

items.title: OpenAI's rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack - Politico
items.summary: GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. A second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models. The powerful artificial intelligence models from OpenAI that went rogue and mounted an unprecedented, autonomous cyberattack earlier this month spent more than four days loose on the internet orchestrating the hack, according to a new analysis from the platform that was breached. Separately, a second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models during the same event, raising questions about how OpenAI failed to detect the alarming activity for days. But in a new analysis published Tuesday, Hugging Face said OpenAI’s two models — one publicly released and a second unreleased — did much more: They carried out 17,600 hacking actions on the internet between July 9 and July 13, during which time the models moved from their first foothold on the open internet to inside Hugging Face’s servers.

items.title: OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center - Insurance Journal
items.summary: # OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center. OpenAI plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on a massive new data center near Savannah, Georgia as part of the ChatGPT maker’s push to keep up with surging demand for artificial intelligence software. The startup has contracted with Georgia Power Co. and secured 3.2 gigawatts of energy for the data center complex in Effingham County, potentially setting the facility up to rank among OpenAI’s largest to date. OpenAI committed to spend $20 billion in the county in order to qualify for an incentive package that will be voted on this week, the company said. The startup is currently looking for partners to help finance and develop the data center, Katti said, and may opt to do some of the operation itself. The company has partnered with developers on large data centers in Europe, the Middle East and several US states as part of its Stargate initiative.

items.title: OpenAI's agents hacked second firm during model testing - Axios
items.summary: OpenAI's models were responsible for another hack on an outside firm, a security executive told Reuters and confirmed to Axios. **Why it matters:** This is the second company that OpenAI's rogue agent system hacked after breaking containment during testing earlier this month. **State of play:** Modal Labs CTO Akshat Bubna told Reuters — and confirmed to Axios — Tuesday that one of its customers' assets was hacked when an OpenAI agent broke into Hugging Face's systems earlier this month. * Hugging Face said in a technical write-up of the hack Monday that when OpenAI's AI agent system broke into its backend, the agent also accessed an isolated testing environment "hosted on a ​third-party provider's infrastructure.". * "We're aware a Modal customer published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution," Bubna said in a statement to Axios. Modal's platform was not compromised in any way.". Modal's infrastructure was not compromised in any way.".

items.title: OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face - WIRED
items.summary: # OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face. OpenAI said Tuesday that the rogue AI agent that breached Hugging Face’s platform also hacked multiple third-party accounts and services as part of the attack. It's now clear that the unprecedented security incident, which arose during an internal test of OpenAI’s latest AI models, was more extensive than the company initially disclosed. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said that an ongoing review of the incident revealed that “four accounts” tied to “publicly available services” were used by the AI agent as part of a larger effort to hack Hugging Face. One of the additional accounts compromised by OpenAI’s agent was used as an “outbound relay and staging path,” potentially to obscure where the attack on Hugging Face was coming from, the company said. Reuters reported on Tuesday that a customer of Modal, a company that offers software infrastructure for training and running AI services, was one of the entities compromised by OpenAI’s agent.
